# Fair Work Ombudsman recovers $453 million for workers, as Booth urges compliance common ground
**14 September 2026**

The Fair Work Ombudsman has announced recoveries of more than $450 million in unpaid wages and entitlements for more than 181,000 workers in 2025-26.

This is an increase of about $95 million on the previous year – up 27 per cent – for the national workplace regulator.

Fair Work Ombudsman Anna Booth said the recovery of $453 million in underpaid wages in the last financial year is a great result for workers.

"These recoveries also help to ensure all those businesses that pay correctly are not at a disadvantage for doing so.

Recoveries from proactive investigations increased to over $45 million for 13,803 workers in 2025-26 (over $10 million more than that 2024-25, where $35.2 million was recovered).

These results occurred after the consistent work FWO has done to create an environment that expects large corporates to prioritise compliance and to report to us when they have got it wrong.

In another priority area, disability support services, the FWO completed more than 1,000 disputes and recovered nearly $24 million for 10,546 workers.

Claire, 0418 825 074, [media@fwo.gov.au](mailto:media@fwo.gov.au)

# $358 million back-paid to Australian workers
The Fair Work Ombudsman recovered $358 million for more than 249,000 underpaid workers in 2024-25, taking back-payments to workers to more than $2 billion across the last five years.

They collectively back-paid almost $213 million to nearly 118,000 underpaid employees.

The workplace regulator also issued 1,220 Compliance Notices, recovering $8.2 million in unpaid wages for 3,438 workers.

FWO helped recover $7.3 million for 2,120 workers through dispute assistance.

Ms Booth said there was plenty more to do in the year to come.
